sentences.text: Judgment:
The appellants are claimants in M.V.O.P.No.307 of 2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge Ongole, and the respondents herein are the respondents in the said case.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge Ongole
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.

3. The claimants are filed a Claim Petition under section 163-A, and 166 of Motor Vehicles Act for seeking compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- for the death of R.Subrahmanyam, in a Motor Vehicle Accident, that occurred on 08.06.2008 at about 06:00 A.M.
4.

The case of the petitioners are as follows:
The deceased was working as Secondary Grade Teacher, ZP High School, he earing Rs.10,497/- per month.

The petitioner further pleaded that on 08.06.2008 at about 06:00 AM., while the deceased along with his family members were returning from Tirupati to Kurnool in the vehicle Tempo Trax bearing No.AP 21 V 7907 and when they reached the out skirts of Kurnool town near Shilpa town ship, the tipper bearing No.AP 21 TT 0110, the 2nd respondent insured with 3rd respondent being driven by its driver 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the vehicular traffic dashed against the tempo trax vehicle in opposite direction resulting which the tempo trax and fell down and inmates of the tempo trax sustained grievous injuries, and one girl and the driver of the tempo trax died on the spot itself.

5. The 1st respondent-driver of the vehicle filed counter denying all the material allegations made in the petition including manner of accident and contended that the accident was not due to his rash and negligent driving but for that of the driver of tempo trax, that 1st respondent was under the employment of 2nd respondent and 1st respondent has no liability to pay compensation.
6. The 2nd respondent owner of the vehicle filed written statement denying all the material allegations made in the petition and contended that 1st respondent was having valid driving license at the time of accident, that there was no negligence on the part of the 1st respondent, that there was Ravinuthala Anitha 2 Others vs Anga Prabhakar 2 Others on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98394797/
1 head on collision between the tipper and the tempo trax, that the owner and insurer of the tempo trax are also proper and necessary parties, that the claim of the petitioners is very excessive.
7. The 3rd respondent filed written statement denying all the material allegations made in the petition including manner of accident, involvement of the vehicle and its owing by 2nd respondent much less with permit and Insurance with 3 rd respondent or its driving by its driver 1st respondent much less with license and contended that there is no rash or negligent driving on the part of 1st respondent, that there is no privity of contract between the parties, that 2nd respondent was not at all the insured as there is variation in respect of the name of the insured in the policy, that the petitioners are not certain about the involvement of the vehicle responsible for the accident whether it was tipper or tractor or truck, that the driver, owner and insurer of the tempo trax vehicle are proper and necessary parties, that the driver of the tempo trax vehicle was not having valid driving license at the time of accident, that more than the permitted number of passengers boarded the tempo trax vehicle, that as per the police records there was a clear head on collision between the two vehicles, thereby there was contributor negligence on the part of the driver of tempo trax vehicle,
that the claim of the petitioners is very excessive and arbitrary and 3 rd respondent is entitled to protection of sec.147, 149 & 170 M.V.Act.
8.

sentences.text:
Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
1) Whether the deceased died due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of R2's crime vehicle or that of the driver of tempo trax or from the contributory negligence of both the drivers of R2 and tempo trax?
2) What is the correct age and income of deceased at the time of accident?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
3) To what relief?
On behalf of the petitioners PW1 is examined and Ex.A1 to A7 are marked.
On behalf of respondents RW1 is examined, Ex.B1 to B3 are marked.
Basing on the material on record, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim application by granting compensation of Rs.6,58,000/-.
Aggrieved by the same the present appeal is preferred by claimants for enhancement of compensation.

9. Now, the point for consideration are:
1) Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference?
2) Whether the claimants are entitled enhanced compensation as prayed for?

sentences.text: In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tipper lorry.

While the deceased along with his family members were returning from Tirupati to Kurnool in tempo trax bearing No.AP 21 V 7907, when they reached the out skirts of Kurnool town near Shilpa Town ship,
the tipper bearing No.AP 21 TT 0110 of 2nd respondent insured with 3rd respondent being driven by its driver 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, without observing the vehicular traffic dashed to the tempo trax and the tempo trax fell down, the passengers in the said tempo trax received injuries.
11. As per the First Information Report, at about 13 persons were travelling in the tempo trax including the driver.
It appears that the over loading of the tempo trax vehicle was also one of the contributory factors for the accident in question.
No doubt, the police filed a charge sheet after completion of investigation against tipper driver.

But some part contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the tempo trax in which the deceased and others were travelling cannot be ignored,
therefore, on considering the evidence on record the contributory negligence on the deceased is fixed at 30% and the negligence on the 1 st respondent tipper driver is fixed at 70%.
12.

No doubt, as per the material on record the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the tipper bearing No. AP 21 TT 0110, but, I have clearly stated above there is a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, because, he opted to travelling the tempo trax, in which 13 passengers are travelling at that time of accident, therefore, the contributory negligence of 30% is fixed on the deceased.

13. As per Ex.A2 and A3 inquest report and PM report, the deceased was aged about 45 years, the oral and documentary evidence and Ex.A6 salary certificate of the deceased, clearly proves that the monthly earning of the deceased Rs.10,497/- per month, and working as a Secondary Grade Teacher in ZP High School, Kothakota, and his net salary was Rs.9,717/- and the Tribunal estimated the net salary of the deceased Rs.9,700/-per month, the same is not disputed by the respondents and no appeal is filed against the said finding.
Here the dependents on the deceased are three persons wife and children of the deceased.
Therefore, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personnel expenses of the deceased (Rs.9,700x12) =Rs.1,16,400/-.

Which is the Annual Net Income of the deceased, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personnel living expenses of the deceased Rs.38,800/- has to deducted from out of Rs.1,16,400/-, therefore, Net Annual Income available to the petitioners is Rs.77,600/-.

As per the decision of Smt. Sarala Varma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another1, the multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased 41 to 45 is '14', therefore,
Rs.77,600x14=10,86,400/- loss of consortium is awarded to the 1st petitioner wife of the 2009 (4)
SCJ 91 deceased Rs.15,000/- and funeral expenses is awarded to the petitioners for an amount of Rs.5,000/-, therefore, in total the petitioners are entitled total compensation of Rs.11,06,400/- from out of which 30% has to be deducted towards contributory negligence of the deceased Rs.11,06,400x30%=3,31,920/- has to be deducted Rs.11,06,400-3,31,920/-=Rs.7,74,480/-.

The petitioners are entitled the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,16,480/- with interest of 9% p.a., as awarded by the Tribunal against the respondents.
Out of the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest, the 1st petitioner is entitled to receive an amount of Rs.66,480/- with total interest.

2nd and 3rd petitioners are entitled to receive an amount of Rs.25,000/- each, since they are the minors, their amount shall be deposited in fixed deposit till the their attaining the majority after attaining majority they are permitted to withdraw the same, the respondents 1 to 3 are directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within one (1) month from the date of the judgment.
As sequel, Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
